mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate at 0.16% (near zero) indicates an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS <= 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 0.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 8.0% and industrial production falls below 96.0, it indicates a deteriorating economic cycle that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0% and INDPRO < 96.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL < 215.0) and low industrial production (INDPRO < 96.0), the economy is in a low-growth phase that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 215.0 and INDPRO < 96.0.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of housing starts (582.0 thousand units) is interpreted as a positive signal for the economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 500.0 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 96.0 and housing starts fall below 550.0, it signals a weak economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 96.0 and HOUST < 550.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 8.0%) with rising employment (PAYEMS > 130000.0), the labor market is recovering, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
